title: How to use the voluntary payrolling benefits and expenses online service
text:
Use this service to register to voluntarily payroll benefits in kind and expenses for your employees.

 You cannot use this service to register to payroll:

 • company cars and fuel

 • company vans and fuel 

 • medical insurance 

 You must report these benefits through your payroll software.

 When to register for voluntary payrolling 

 You need to register to voluntarily payroll benefits before the start of the relevant tax year.

 You cannot change the way you report benefits and expenses for the current tax year.

 What you can do in the service

 In the service you can:

 • register to voluntarily payroll benefits and expenses for the next tax year

 • cancel your registration to voluntarily payroll benefits and expenses

 • view benefits registered to payroll voluntarily for the current tax year

 • view employees who have been excluded from a payrolled benefit

 • exclude employees from a payrolled benefit for the current tax year

 Register for voluntary payrolling

 If you’re an employer, use the payrolling benefits and expenses online service .

 If you’re an agent, sign in to your HMRC online services account — you can access the payrolling benefits online service through the PAYE for agents online service.

 Check if there are any problems with the payrolling benefits and expenses service .

 How voluntary payrolling works

 Up to and including 5 April 2027

 For benefits you already voluntarily payroll, follow the existing rules for the tax year 2026 to 2027.

 You must:

 • add the cash equivalent of the employees’ benefits to their pay

 • deduct Income Tax through payroll

 • work out Class 1A National Insurance contributions and complete form P11D(b) 

 You do not need to report the payrolled benefit on form P11D.

 From 6 April 2027

 For benefits you’re registered to voluntarily payroll, you must: 

 • add the cash equivalent of the employees’ benefits to their pay 

 • deduct Income Tax and account for any associated Class 1A National Insurance contributions in real time using payroll software 

 You will not need to report payrolled benefits through the P11D and P11D(b) forms.

 HMRC will make sure the value of the benefit is not included in your employees’ tax codes.

 Find out more about voluntarily payrolling employee benefits and expenses .

 If you provide benefits that have not been payrolled

 You will need to submit electronic P11Ds for any employees where you have provided benefits which have not been payrolled.

 You can exclude employees from a voluntarily payrolled benefit, but you’ll need to use form P11D to declare the non-payrolled benefits. Once you’ve excluded an employee, you cannot add them back to a benefit in the same tax year.
changeNote: The service has reopened for registrations and cancellations. Living accommodation and loans can now be payrolled. Guidance on how voluntary payrolling will work from 6 April 2027 has been added.
